Subject: Re: BrightLane PoC — intermittent failed requests after long idle periods

Quick field note — I reproduced the issue locally against a Dedicated-like config yesterday. Observed behavior: after ~25–40 minutes of inactivity the downstream connection pool returns a stale connection; the runtime then fails the inflight request rather than transparently reestablishing the KV cache state.

Workaround I used: the JS SDK can be configured to emit a light keepalive (empty heartbeat request every 10 minutes). This keeps the pool from pruning the connection for most cases. Caveats: additional traffic and token counts — cost impact depends on volume. Also defeats some idle-scaling savings.

This sounds like a runtime connection-lease vs. token TTL mismatch. Putting on Dev/Runtime to confirm exact mechanisms.

—Karthik

Subject: Re: BrightLane PoC — intermittent failed requests after long idle periods

Thanks for the repro and the logs — I pulled session-logs.zip. Short technical summary from runtime:

- We have two separate TTLs in play: the auth token TTL (default 1h) and an internal connection lease TTL (default 20m). The connection lease is a server-side handle we use to keep KV cache and kernel residency hot for that client session. When the lease expires we clean local cache and the next request must warm the model state; currently the runtime returns an error path fast to avoid head-of-line blocking for other clients.

- The SDK currently does not expose an explicit lease-extension API. It relies on natural traffic to bump the lease.

Immediate options:
1) Short-term mitigation: SDK keepalive ping every 10m. Simple, low risk. Trade-off: increased token/compute usage, may affect cost and autoscaler behavior.
2) Short-term mitigation: client retry with a warmed fallback route — the runtime can accept the request and re-warm the KV cache in the background while returning a partial-progress indication. That requires changes to request flow and is non-trivial.
3) Medium-term: bump default connection lease to 8h for Dedicated and Hosted 2.1.x patch. This reduces occurrence but increases memory footprint on nodes (risk for very large scale clusters).

Proposed immediate action: ship an SDK patch (patch/minor) that exposes a "lease_keepalive_interval_ms" option with a safe default of 0 (off) and an explicit doc recommending 10m for low-volume interactive apps. We'll open SUP-1234 and schedule a controlled rollout to Dedicated tenants first.

Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-1234
Notes: we should include telemetry to measure additional idle traffic and memory impact during the rollout.

Let me know if Product wants us to expose this option; we'll push a patch in the next two weeks if approved.

—Dev

Thanks everyone for the triage. Decision notes:

- Approve exposing a controlled SDK parameter lease_keepalive_interval_ms with default 0. Add guardrails: doc clearly marked "not recommended for high-throughput services" and server-side quota for keepalive pings (to avoid abuse).
- Prioritize a patch release for SDK within 10 business days; runtime will ship a follow-up config change (bump to 8h) for Dedicated in the next minor if telemetry looks good.
- No SLA credit decision yet — Marissa, please work with Legal/Support and BrightLane procurement (contract@brightlane.com) and circle back. If this caused a production-visible outage during a paid demo window, we may need an exception.

Marissa: coordinate the customer message. Sean: please confirm the wording I should use for the release notes and recommended mitigation. Dev: please create the SUP ticket and include rollout telemetry hooks.
